title: Read-Heavy Social Feed with Hot Partition Fan-Out
subtitle: Hybrid Fan-out-on-Write vs Fan-out-on-Read with Celebrity Partitioning
problem_statement: A social network platform with 100 million users generates user timelines. The system uses a pure Fan-Out-On-Write (push) model where every new post is copied into all followers' timeline lists in Redis. When a celebrity account with 40 million followers posts, the write pipeline spikes by 40 million insert operations, exhausting Redis memory and lagging normal users' feeds by 45 minutes.

faded_bug.description: Unconditional push fan-out for accounts with millions of followers creates massive write amplification and Redis starvation.

invariants.description: Feed retrieval P99 latency must not exceed 30ms even during celebrity post publish.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Compare Fan-Out-On-Write (push) vs Fan-Out-On-Read (pull) models in terms of write latency, storage cost, and timeline assembly time.
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: How does your hybrid engine merge a user's pre-computed Redis inbox with 15 followed celebrity timelines at request time in less than 20ms?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: A user follows 2,000 celebrities. During a major sporting event, all 2,000 celebrities post concurrently. How do you prevent K-way merge degradation?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: Inactive users (who haven't opened the app in 30 days) consume 80% of your Redis RAM in pre-computed feeds. Design a timeline eviction and cold-storage hydration tier.

counter_probes.counter_question: When an account with 50M followers posts, you must execute 50M write operations. At 100,000 writes/sec, that takes 500 seconds. How do you explain an 8-minute delay for followers?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: Push-only model collapses on asymmetric follow graphs. A hybrid architecture that treats accounts with >25k followers as pull-based and executes an in-memory merge at read time is mandatory.
